piece_type: DTC video “An Oprah Special: Shame, Blame, and the Weight Loss Revolution” (ABC primetime 3/18/2024; Hulu) featuring paid consultants and a Novo Nordisk sales executive

cases.claim: [Omission] Boxed-warning MEN 2 contraindication (only “anybody [who] has a history specifically of medullary thyroid cancer,” discussed); Wegovy W&Ps omitted: hypoglycemia, acute kidney injury, hypersensitivity, diabetic retinopathy complications, heart rate increase, suicidal behavior and ideation; Ozempic: diabetic retinopathy, pen sharing, hypoglycemia, AKI, hypersensitivity; Victoza W&Ps
cases.context: Paid consultants' benefit claims (“essentially copying what our normal GLP-1 hormone does in our body, but doing it a little bit better.”; “double the amount of weight loss.”) attributed to Novo; teen Victoza testimonial; FDA prior comments to Novo.
cases.rationale: Omits boxed-warning element and multiple W&Ps.
cases.check: Rule: diff risk content vs boxed warning populations and MG side-effect lists for every product discussed.

cases.claim: “There’s been a lot of hype around like pancreatitis, gallbladder complications, concerns for thyroid cancer. This has really not been shown in human studies that this is a downstream complication, and that really the risk is less than 1%.” | “If anybody has a history specifically of MTC... is very, very rare. ... recognizing that it’s rare, but it’s there and we have to always screen.”
cases.context: Victoza PI: “cases of MTC have been reported in the postmarketing period in patients treated with Victoza”; acute pancreatitis incl. fatal hemorrhagic/necrotizing observed with semaglutide.
cases.check: Rule: lexicon flag — 'hype', 'very rare', 'not been shown in human studies' near boxed-warning/W&P terms.

cases.claim: “I think that they’ve gotten overhyped. Medicines have side effects, but the important part is that they’re mild to moderate in the research studies.”
cases.context: Response to a patient who discontinued a GLP-1 due to side effects.
cases.rationale: Characterizes risks as overhyped and mild-to-moderate when not demonstrated.
cases.check: Rule: flag 'overhyped' / 'mild to moderate' / 'medicines have side effects' framings.

cases.cat: Lack of fair balance / risk prominence
cases.claim: [Format] of a 42-minute video, only four minutes devoted to shared GLP-1 risks, relegated to the end; no signal where to find more risk information
cases.rationale: Risk not reasonably comparable in prominence to benefits.
cases.check: Rule: compute risk vs benefit airtime ratio and placement.

cases.cat: Failure to submit at first use (Form FDA 2253)
cases.claim: [Process] video not submitted under Form FDA 2253 at initial publication
cases.context: Third-party program attributed to company via paid consultants and executive.
cases.check: Process rule: inventory consultant/executive media appearances for 2253.
